title: Proof-of-value: dedicated sizing simulation notes
content:
Purpose
-----
Quick proof-of-value (PoV) simulation and deployment recommendation for Customer-Alpha: estimate dedicated GPU pool size, autoscale policy draft, and back-of-envelope GPU cost estimates to support a 99th-percentile latency SLO of 300ms for generation endpoints. This is an operational working note — rough sims, assumptions, and open questions included.

Customer context and constraints
-------------------------------
- Customer-Alpha: fintech SaaS, US + EU traffic, strict PII isolation requirement => Dedicated capacity (no shared multi-tenant).
- Peak traffic expected after activation: ~120 RPS of user-facing completion calls (95% text-gen, 5% embeddings) across both regions, expected growth 30% q/q during PoV.
- Typical prompt length: 120 tokens in, 220 tokens out (median). Service pattern: sync HTTP + streaming supported for web UI.
- Latency SLO: p99 <= 300ms for typical requests (where typical = 220 output tokens). Budget constraint: target < $10k/mo for PoV (ops + infra) — flexible if justified.

Workload model and simulation assumptions
----------------------------------------
- Workload: non-bursty baseline with occasional peaks (factor 3 for 3–5 minutes every few hours). Simulated with Poisson arrivals plus 10% chance of short spike.
- Request profile: average tokens generated = 220, average compute per token ~ 0.00035 GPU-seconds/token on A100-80 (baseline kernel + kv cache misses).
- KV cache warmup: assume 60% KV hit after steady-state warm caches for customer workload; cold-starts for new conversations reduce hit rate to 20% for first 10 requests per session.
- Batch window target: 25ms (aggressive), max latency budget for batching = 60ms; effective batching factor depends on arrival rate.
- Model choices: rwd-1-large (approx equivalently sized to 7B family) and rwd-1-small (1.7B) as fallback/low-cost variant.
- GPU types evaluated: A10G (24GB), A100-80GB. Hourly spot/on-demand pricing used for baseline (sensitive): A10G on-demand $0.95/hr, A100-80 $3.40/hr (cloud list prices, region-adjusted later).

Simulation summary (high level)
------------------------------
I ran three scenarios: conservative steady, peak-dominant, and growth-adjusted. Key outputs below are per-region estimates (US region example).

Scenario A — steady (120 RPS baseline, 1.0x peak):
- Effective qps after embeddings: 114 RPS gen traffic (excludes low-latency metadata calls).
- Average batch size observed (25ms window): ~6 tokens-requests aggregated -> effective throughput ~360 tokens/second per GPU core equivalent.
- GPU count (A100-80) to keep p99 < 300ms: 4 GPUs (dedicated pool), with a small warm standby pool (0.5 GPU equivalent) for quick bursts.
- Estimated infra cost (A100-80 on-demand): 4 * $3.40/hr * 24 * 30 = $9,792/mo (base). Add ~15% for networking/storage/other infra => ~$11,260/mo.

Scenario B — peak (3x spikes for short windows):
- To meet spikes without violating p99, need burst lanes (ephemeral on-demand or pre-warmed instances). Option A: maintain 6 GPUs baseline to absorb typical spikes -> ~$16,884/mo. Option B (recommended for PoV): keep 4 GPUs baseline + 3 pre-warmed burst GPUs with fast scale-in/out (scale-in cooldown 300s) and use A10G spot when possible -> blended cost ~ $12.5k/mo (est, depends on spot reliability).

Scenario C — cost-optimized (use rwd-1-small fallback, aggressive caching):
- Run 3 A100 GPUs for baseline, route 30% of low-complexity traffic to small model, and implement prefix caching -> estimated infra cost ~$7.2k/mo but observed median latency increases for fallback traffic to ~420ms p99 (not meeting SLO).

Autoscaling policy (draft)
-------------------------
Goal: keep pool small for cost but avoid SLO violations. Two-tier autoscale model: warm pool + burst lane + model fallback.
- Metrics: queue length (requests waiting), GPU utilization (avg over 15s), p99 serving latency (real-time).
- Scale-out rule (fast): if queued requests > 12 OR GPU util > 85% for 15s -> add 1 GPU (up to burst limit).
- Warm-target: maintain at least 60% of baseline node count warm (to ensure KV caches are hot for customer workload). Warm nodes are kept idle but pre-initialized (costly but reduces cold-start p99 penalty).
- Burst lane: allow up to +3 ephemeral GPUs for short spikes; these can be spot/A10G to reduce cost. Ephemeral pool scaled down immediately after spike (cooldown 300s) unless p99 latency remains degraded.
- Fallback policy: when infra constrained or spot failures, route small-model for up to 40% of traffic with dynamic A/B weight and degrade quality gracefully (metrics: coherence delta, hallucination increase). Auto-fallback must be gated by QA eval set (see linked eval ticket).

Operational considerations and runbook bullets
---------------------------------------------
- Canary deployment: gradual traffic shift 0->50% small-model over 10 minutes, measure latency and quality metrics (BLEU-like and custom regressions).
- Observability: instrument per-model, per-customer cost metrics; trace token-level latency and KV hit rate. Add quick Grafana dashboard for p99 per-route and node churn.
- Cost control: set hard limit on ephemeral burst usage (max 120 GPU-hours/day) to avoid runaway costs during misconfiguration.
- Security: ensure private VPC and KMS policies are in place for keys; per-customer isolation required by contract.

Back-of-envelope per-token cost example
-------------------------------------
- Using A100 baseline and observed throughput, estimated cost-per-output-token (infra only) = (A100 $3.40/hr) / (avg tokens generated per GPU-hour ~ 2.8M) = $1.21e-6 per token. With caching improvements (~+35% effective throughput) this drops to ~$8e-7/token. Add model licensing and infra overhead => estimate $1.6e-6/token.

Risks and unknowns
-------------------
- KV hit-rate variability: we assumed 60% steady-state; if real traffic is far more diverse, effective throughput drops 30–50% and GPU counts must increase accordingly.
- Spot capacity reliability and A10G performance variance across regions.
- Customer may require stricter P99 (150ms) that would require significantly more GPUs or smaller models.
- Real model perf numbers (tokens/sec) depend on model kernels and quantization; need engineering perf runs for the exact customer model sizes.

Open questions / action items
-----------------------------
- [Aisha] Schedule benchmark run: run customer prompt-set on rwd-1-large and rwd-1-small end-to-end on both A100 and A10G (perf + KV behavior). Target date: 2024-11-15.
- [Marcus] Confirm region pricing for dedicated instances (us-east1 and eu-west1) and provide spot reliability stats by 2024-11-10.
- [Priya] Prepare a short customer-facing one-pager with recommended baseline + burst lane options and cost ranges (two sided: conservative / cost-optimized) for PoV kickoff.
- [Jonah] Create evaluation harness (Confluence + GitHub) that can run the QA prompt-set and produce coherence/quality deltas for fallback routing. Link: GH PR created above.

Appendix: quick sim parameters (for reproducibility)
---------------------------------------------------
- Arrival process: Poisson with lambda = 120 RPS; spike event: every 3–6 hours, multiply lambda by 3 for duration sampled Uniform(180s, 300s).
- Token compute: baseline 0.00035 GPU-seconds/token (A100), small-model 0.00012 GPU-seconds/token.
- Batch-window 25ms, batching efficiency multiplier = 0.8 on small batches <3.
- KV warmup: per-session warm period: first 10 requests 20% hit, afterwards 60% hit.

Notes to self (informal)
-----------------------
- Customer will push back on $11k/mo estimate; prepare a side-by-side with a hybrid dedicated+private-edge plan.
- Consider recommending a 3-month PoV with 4 A100 baseline + burst as compromise; present monthly burn + expected ramp to justify reserve.
- Re-check A10G perf for streaming workloads; streaming changes batching dynamics a lot.

End of note.
